title: Rehost a Server with AWS MGN
goal: Goal: Rehost an on-premises host server to AWS EC2 using AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) continuous block replication.

concepts.title: Rehosting (Lift-and-Shift)
concepts.body: Moving servers to AWS EC2 without altering application code or architecture.

concepts.title: AWS MGN
concepts.body: Primary AWS service for continuous block-level server replication and automated migrations.

concepts.title: Staging Subnet
concepts.body: A private subnet where lightweight MGN replication servers receive continuous disk block updates.

whyItMatters: This matters because AWS MGN is the primary exam answer for automated, low-downtime server migrations to AWS EC2.
costWarning: Application Migration Service replication infrastructure, staging resources, EC2 instances, EBS volumes, snapshots and data-transfer charges may apply.

consoleSteps.title: Initialize AWS Application Migration Service

instructions.text: Open Application Migration Service.
Choose Region us-east-1.
Choose Get started.
Select your lab VPC and private staging subnet.
Choose Save replication template.

consoleSteps.note: Initializes service-linked roles and default staging subnet settings.

consoleSteps.title: Create installer IAM user and credentials

instructions.text: Open IAM.
Choose Users -> Create user.
Name user mgn-agent-installer.
Attach policy AWSApplicationMigrationAgentInstallationPolicy.
Open Security credentials -> Create access key -> Choose CLI.
Copy Access Key ID and Secret Access Key.

consoleSteps.note: Allows the agent to register the source server with MGN.

consoleSteps.title: Install AWS Replication Agent on source server

instructions.text: Connect to your source server (Linux or Windows).
Download installer: wget https://aws-application-migration-service-us-east-1.s3.amazonaws.com/latest/linux/aws-replication-installer-init.py.
Run script: sudo python3 aws-replication-installer-init.py.
Enter Region us-east-1, Access Key ID, and Secret Access Key.
Confirm default disk selection.

consoleSteps.note: Starts continuous block-level disk replication.

consoleSteps.title: Monitor replication and launch test instance

instructions.text: Open MGN -> Source servers.
Select your registered server hostname.
Confirm replication status displays Healthy and Ready for testing.
Choose Test and cutover -> Launch test instances.
Verify test EC2 instance in the EC2 console.

consoleSteps.note: Testing does not interrupt continuous replication.

consoleSteps.title: Perform cutover and tear down resources

instructions.text: Select source server in MGN.
Choose Test and cutover -> Mark as ready for cutover.
Choose Test and cutover -> Launch cutover instances.
Choose Finalize cutover.
Terminate test/cutover EC2 instances and delete mgn-agent-installer IAM user.

consoleSteps.warning: Terminate test instances and delete server record when finished to avoid charges.

title: Database Migration & Schema Conversion with AWS DMS & SCT
goal: Goal: Migrate an on-premises database (e.g. MySQL or PostgreSQL) to Amazon RDS/Aurora with minimal downtime using AWS DMS and SCT.

concepts.title: AWS DMS (Database Migration Service)
concepts.body: Migrates relational databases, NoSQL databases, and data warehouses to AWS with minimal application downtime.

concepts.title: AWS SCT (Schema Conversion Tool)
concepts.body: Converts source database schemas, views, and stored procedures to match heterogeneous target database engines (e.g., Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL).

concepts.title: Homogeneous vs Heterogeneous Migration
concepts.body: Homogeneous: Same source and target engine (e.g. MySQL to RDS MySQL). SCT not required. Heterogeneous: Different engines (e.g. Oracle to PostgreSQL). SCT converts schema first.

concepts.title: Full Load + CDC (Change Data Capture)
concepts.body: Full Load copies existing table records. CDC continuously captures ongoing transaction binlogs until cutover.

concepts.title: DMS Migration Setup Plan
concepts.body: ComponentLab valuePurposeReplication instancesaa-dms-instance (dms.t3.micro)Runs migration engineSource endpointsaa-source-db (MySQL 3306)Points to source databaseTarget endpointsaa-target-db (Amazon RDS MySQL 3306)Points to target RDS databaseMigration task typeFull load + CDCInitial load + ongoing changesFree Tier emulationEC2 Single-AZ MySQL + Single-AZ RDS MySQLZero cost under Free Tier

whyItMatters: This matters because AWS DMS combined with SCT allows database migrations with virtually zero application downtime and is a major topic on SAA-C03.
costWarning: DMS replication resources, serverless capacity, logging, storage, database and data-transfer charges may apply.

consoleSteps.title: Set up the lab user and permissions

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console.
Sign in to the AWS Management Console using an IAM user or lab role with appropriate permissions.
Sign in to the AWS Management Console using an IAM user or lab role with appropriate permissions.
For least privilege, use the grouped permissions below.

consoleSteps.note: Identity check: sts:GetCallerIdentity DMS setup: dms:CreateReplicationInstance, dms:CreateEndpoint, dms:CreateReplicationTask, dms:TestConnection RDS setup: rds:CreateDBInstance, rds:DescribeDBInstances Cleanup: dms:DeleteReplicationTask, dms:DeleteEndpoint, dms:DeleteReplicationInstance, rds:DeleteDBInstance
consoleSteps.warning: Do not leave broad admin access or long-term access keys in real company accounts.

consoleSteps.title: Provision Source and Target Databases (Free Tier Emulation)

instructions.text: Open Amazon RDS -> Choose Create database.
Select MySQL engine -> Choose Free tier template.
Set DB instance identifier to saa-dms-target-db, master username to admin, and password.
Set Instance class to db.t3.micro (Free Tier eligible) and choose Create database.
Emulate the source database by running MySQL on a free t3.micro EC2 instance (or local container).
Ensure binary logging is enabled on source MySQL (binlog_format=ROW) to allow CDC transaction capture.

consoleSteps.note: Binary logging (binlog) is required on source databases for DMS Change Data Capture (CDC).

consoleSteps.title: Convert schema using AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT)

instructions.text: For Homogeneous migrations (e.g. MySQL to RDS MySQL): Use native mysqldump or pg_dump to export and import schema directly.
For Heterogeneous migrations (e.g. Oracle / SQL Server to PostgreSQL / Aurora): Download and launch AWS SCT.
Create a new SCT project -> Connect to Source DB -> Connect to Target RDS DB.
Choose Convert Schema -> Review Schema Transformation Report -> Choose Apply to database.

consoleSteps.note: SCT converts DDL statements, indexes, views, and stored procedures across different engine dialects.

consoleSteps.title: Create AWS DMS Replication Instance

instructions.text: Open Database Migration Service (DMS).
In the left sidebar, click Replication instances -> Choose Create replication instance.
Set Name to saa-dms-instance.
Set Replication instance class to dms.t3.micro (Free Tier eligible).
Select your VPC and replication subnet group.
Keep Multi-AZ set to Single-AZ to avoid extra charges.
Choose Create replication instance.

consoleSteps.note: The replication instance runs the DMS engine that reads source logs and writes to the target.

consoleSteps.title: Create Source and Target DMS Endpoints

instructions.text: Open DMS -> Endpoints -> Choose Create endpoint.
Source Endpoint: Choose Source endpoint -> Set Identifier saa-source-endpoint -> Engine MySQL -> Input Source IP/DNS, Port 3306, username, and password -> Choose Test endpoint connection.
Target Endpoint: Choose Target endpoint -> Set Identifier saa-target-endpoint -> Check Select RDS DB instance -> Choose saa-dms-target-db -> Input password -> Choose Test endpoint connection.
Ensure both endpoint connections display successful.

consoleSteps.note: Endpoints store connection parameters and credentials for DMS to communicate with databases.

consoleSteps.title: Create and execute Full Load + CDC Replication Task

instructions.text: Open DMS -> Database migration tasks -> Choose Create task.
Set Task identifier to saa-dms-migration-task.
Select Replication instance saa-dms-instance, Source endpoint saa-source-endpoint, and Target endpoint saa-target-endpoint.
Under Migration type, select Migrate existing data and replicate ongoing changes (Full load + CDC).
Under Table mappings, choose Wizard -> Add selection rule -> Schema % -> Table % -> Action Include.
Choose Create task.
Monitor Task status transitioning: Starting → Full load complete → Replication ongoing.
Perform cutover once CDC latency drops to 0 seconds.

consoleSteps.note: Full load copies initial table contents; CDC streams live binlog transactions continuously.

consoleSteps.title: Tear down resources in dependency order

instructions.text: Select saa-dms-migration-task -> Choose Actions -> Stop -> then Delete.
Select source and target endpoints -> Choose Delete.
Select saa-dms-instance -> Choose Delete.
Open RDS -> Select saa-dms-target-db -> Choose Actions -> Delete (uncheck final snapshot for lab cleanup).
Terminate any source EC2 instance used for emulation.

consoleSteps.warning: Delete the DMS replication instance and RDS database when finished to prevent continuous hourly charges.

cheatSheet.title: AWS DMS (Database Migration)
cheatSheet.body: Migrates databases (homogeneous or heterogeneous) with minimal downtime. Requires a Replication Instance, Source Endpoint, and Target Endpoint.

cheatSheet.title: AWS SCT (Schema Conversion)
cheatSheet.body: Converts source DB schema (tables, views, stored procedures) to target engine dialect during heterogeneous migrations.

cheatSheet.title: Full Load vs CDC
cheatSheet.body: Full Load: Copies existing data snapshot. CDC (Change Data Capture): Continuously streams ongoing binlog updates.

troubleshooting.title: CDC Replication Failing
troubleshooting.body: Verify binary logging (`binlog_format=ROW`) is enabled on the source MySQL database and that the DMS IAM user has `REPLICATION CLIENT` privileges.

troubleshooting.title: Endpoint Test Connection Failed
troubleshooting.body: Check Security Group rules. Ensure the DMS Replication Instance security group allows outbound traffic to source and target DB ports (3306).

examTraps.title: SCT vs DMS Usage
examTraps.body: DMS does not convert schema definitions for heterogeneous migrations. You MUST use AWS SCT to convert schema before running DMS.

examTraps.title: Homogeneous Migration Shortcuts
examTraps.body: For homogeneous migrations (e.g. MySQL to RDS MySQL), SCT is NOT required. You can use native DB tools (e.g. `mysqldump`) or DMS alone.

examTips.text: SAA-C03: Master AWS Database Migration Service concepts and hybrid connectivity patterns in AWS Database Migration Service.

concepts.title: AWS DMS Replication Instance
concepts.body: Managed EC2 instance running AWS DMS migration software that connects to source/target endpoints, extracts data, and loads records.

concepts.title: DMS Endpoints

concepts.title: Full Load + CDC (Change Data Capture)

concepts.title: Homogeneous vs Heterogeneous
concepts.body: DMS natively migrates homogeneous databases (e.g. MySQL to RDS MySQL). Heterogeneous migrations (e.g. Oracle to Aurora) require AWS SCT for schema conversion.

concepts.title: DMS Migration Architecture Plan

title: Homogeneous vs Heterogeneous Database Migration
goal: Goal: Operational workflow comparing same-engine migrations (DMS alone) vs. engine changes (Oracle/SQL Server to Postgres/Aurora requiring AWS Schema Conversion Tool).

concepts.title: Homogeneous Migration
concepts.body: Source and target database engines are identical (e.g. MySQL to RDS MySQL, Oracle to RDS Oracle). Schemas match natively; AWS SCT is NOT required.

concepts.title: Heterogeneous Migration
concepts.body: Source and target database engines are different (e.g. Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL, SQL Server to MySQL). Schemas and SQL dialects MUST be converted using AWS SCT.

concepts.title: AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT)
concepts.body: Converts source database schemas, views, indexes, stored procedures, and DDL statements into the target engine dialect automatically.

concepts.title: SCT Assessment Report
concepts.body: Generates a detailed report identifying code items that require manual conversion assistance (e.g., complex stored procedures or proprietary functions).

concepts.title: Homogeneous vs Heterogeneous Decision Matrix
concepts.body: FeatureHomogeneous MigrationHeterogeneous MigrationEngine alignmentSame source and target (e.g. Postgres -> RDS Postgres)Different source and target (e.g. SQL Server -> Aurora)Schema tool needed?No (Schemas match natively)YES — AWS SCT RequiredData migration toolAWS DMS or native backup tools (`pg_dump`/`mysqldump`)AWS DMS (Data migration after SCT schema conversion)Stored procedure conversionAutomatic (Identical dialect)AWS SCT converts or flags for manual review

whyItMatters: This matters because knowing exactly when AWS SCT is required alongside AWS DMS is a classic SAA-C03 exam scenario.

title: Large-Scale Offline Data Transfer with AWS Snow Family & S3
goal: Goal: Architect and simulate large-scale offline data ingestion into Amazon S3 using AWS Snowball Edge, S3 Lifecycle archiving rules, and EventBridge validation.

concepts.title: AWS Snowball Edge (Offline Transfer)
concepts.body: Physical rugged appliance used to transport multi-terabyte or petabyte datasets to AWS offline when network transfer over WAN takes weeks or months.

concepts.title: Data Transfer Threshold Rules
concepts.body: Online (AWS DataSync / Direct Connect): Best under 10–20 TB on high bandwidth. Snowball Edge Storage Optimized: Best for 10 TB – 80 TB per device. Snowmobile: For petabyte to exabyte scale (up to 100 PB per truck).

concepts.title: S3 Lifecycle Transition Rules
concepts.body: Automatically transitions uploaded data from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Flexible Archive or S3 Glacier Deep Archive to minimize long-term storage costs.

concepts.title: EventBridge Automated Validation
concepts.body: Fires real-time event notifications whenever new S3 objects land via Snowball to trigger downstream processing or compliance auditing.

concepts.title: Snow Family Transfer Thresholds Plan
concepts.body: Transfer MethodData VolumeNetwork BandwidthPrimary Use CaseAWS DataSync / AWS CLI< 10 TBHigh (1 Gbps+)Online continuous file syncSnowconeUp to 8 TBOffline / EdgeSmall portable physical transferSnowball Edge Storage Optimized10 TB – 80 TBOffline (Shipment)Large offline bulk data migrationSnowmobile> 10 PBOffline (Container truck)Exabyte-scale datacenter migration

whyItMatters: This matters because SAA-C03 exam questions routinely test data volume thresholds (e.g. 10–50+ TB over slow WAN links) to determine when physical Snowball devices are required instead of online streaming.
costWarning: Snow Family job, device, shipping, service-day and data-transfer charges may apply.

consoleSteps.title: Simulate an AWS Snowball Edge Job Order

instructions.text: Open AWS Snow Family Console.
Choose Region us-east-1.
Choose Create job.
Select job type Import into Amazon S3.
Select device type Snowball Edge Storage Optimized (80 TB usable capacity).
Specify shipping address details and shipping speed options.
Select or create target S3 bucket saa-snow-migration-vault-[account-id].
Review job settings (cancel or exit before final order submission to keep your balance at $0).

consoleSteps.note: Ordering physical Snowball devices incurs service fees. Always stop at the summary page during lab practice.

consoleSteps.title: Create Destination S3 Storage Bucket

instructions.text: Open Amazon S3 -> Choose Create bucket.
Set Bucket name to saa-snow-migration-vault-[account-id].
Set Region to us-east-1.
Keep Block Public Access enabled.
Enable Bucket Versioning (recommended for audit trails during large data imports).
Choose Create bucket.

consoleSteps.note: This bucket serves as the landing location when AWS ingests data from returned Snowball devices.

consoleSteps.title: Configure S3 Lifecycle Rule for Immediate Glacier Archiving

instructions.text: Select bucket saa-snow-migration-vault-[account-id] -> Choose Management tab.
Click Create lifecycle rule.
Set Lifecycle rule name to ArchiveSnowballImports.
Choose Apply to all objects in the bucket.
Check Move current versions of objects between storage classes.
Select Glacier Deep Archive -> Set Days after object creation to 1 (or minimum allowed).
Choose Create rule.

consoleSteps.note: Lifecycle rules automatically transition uploaded data to lowest-cost Glacier storage classes.

consoleSteps.title: Configure EventBridge Trigger for Automated Validation

instructions.text: Open Amazon EventBridge -> Choose Rules -> Create rule.
Set Name to catch-snowball-s3-upload.
Select Rule with an event pattern -> Event source AWS services -> Service S3 -> Event type Amazon S3 Event Notification.
Set Target to CloudWatch log group or SNS Topic saa-snow-alerts.
Choose Create rule.

consoleSteps.note: Fires automated triggers whenever new objects land in the destination S3 bucket.

consoleSteps.title: Test Data Upload and Verify Lifecycle Transition

instructions.text: Open Amazon S3 -> Open saa-snow-migration-vault-[account-id].
Upload a sample test file snowball-import-test.txt.
Verify object storage class displays Standard, then inspect Lifecycle rule status.
Open EventBridge / CloudWatch logs to verify real-time event capture.

consoleSteps.note: Simulates data arriving in S3 from a completed Snowball job.

consoleSteps.title: Tear down lab resources in dependency order

instructions.text: Delete test objects from S3 bucket saa-snow-migration-vault-[account-id].
Delete the S3 bucket.
Delete the EventBridge rule catch-snowball-s3-upload.
Cancel any draft Snowball job order.

consoleSteps.warning: Delete S3 buckets and EventBridge rules to clean up your lab environment.

title: Hybrid File Storage Bridge with AWS Storage Gateway
goal: Goal: Deploy an AWS S3 File Gateway to provide on-premises legacy applications with low-latency NFS/SMB access to Amazon S3 storage.

concepts.title: AWS S3 File Gateway (NFS / SMB)
concepts.body: Provides file-based protocol access (NFS v3/v4.1 or SMB) to store files as native objects in Amazon S3 with low-latency local caching.

concepts.title: Volume Gateway (Cached vs Stored iSCSI)
concepts.body: Cached Volumes: Primary data stored in S3; frequent data cached locally. Stored Volumes: Primary data stored locally; asynchronous backup to S3.

concepts.title: Tape Gateway (iSCSI VTL)
concepts.body: Replaces physical tape libraries with virtual tapes in S3 Glacier/Glacier Deep Archive for long-term backup software compliance.

concepts.title: FSx File Gateway
concepts.body: Provides low-latency local caching for cloud-native Amazon FSx for Windows File Server shares.

concepts.title: Storage Gateway Appliance Types Plan
concepts.body: Gateway TypeProtocolBackend StoragePrimary Use CaseS3 File GatewayNFS / SMBAmazon S3 objectsHybrid file storage & S3 ingestFSx File GatewaySMBAmazon FSx for WindowsOn-prem cache for Windows FSxVolume Gateway (Cached)iSCSI blockAmazon S3 + EBS cacheLow-cost cloud block storageVolume Gateway (Stored)iSCSI blockOn-prem disk + S3 backupLocal primary block + cloud backupTape GatewayiSCSI VTLS3 Glacier / Deep ArchiveLegacy backup tape replacement

whyItMatters: This matters because SAA-C03 exam questions frequently test distinguishing between File Gateway (NFS/SMB file shares), Volume Gateway (iSCSI block storage), and Tape Gateway (virtual tape library).
costWarning: Free Tier eligible: AWS Storage Gateway charges $0 for the first gateway created per account. Gateway software is free. To run a lab at $0 cost, launch a free t3.small EC2 instance using the official Storage Gateway AMI, attach a small 150 GB EBS volume for local cache, create an NFS file share mapped to a free S3 bucket, and delete all resources after testing.

consoleSteps.title: Deploy Storage Gateway Appliance Host on EC2

instructions.text: Open AWS Storage Gateway Console -> Choose Create gateway.
Set Gateway name to saa-s3-file-gateway.
Select Gateway type Amazon S3 File Gateway.
Select Host platform Amazon EC2 -> Choose Launch instance.
In the EC2 launch wizard, select the official Storage Gateway AMI, instance type t3.small (or t3.medium), attach an extra 150 GB EBS volume for local cache, and launch.
Note the public/private IP address of your gateway EC2 instance.

consoleSteps.note: Storage Gateway runs as a virtual appliance on VMware ESXi, Hyper-V, KVM, or Amazon EC2.

consoleSteps.title: Activate Storage Gateway and Allocate Local Cache Disk

instructions.text: Return to Storage Gateway Console -> Input your gateway instance IP address -> Choose Activate gateway.
Set Gateway name to saa-s3-file-gateway and choose activation time zone.
In the Configure local disks panel, locate the 150 GB EBS volume and set its allocated usage to Cache.
Choose Save and continue.

consoleSteps.note: Local cache provides low-latency read/write performance for recently accessed files.

consoleSteps.title: Create NFS File Share Mapped to S3 Bucket

instructions.text: Open Storage Gateway -> Choose File shares -> Click Create file share.
Enter Amazon S3 bucket name saa-file-gateway-bridge-[account-id].
Select File share protocol NFS (Network File System).
Select Gateway saa-s3-file-gateway.
Choose Create IAM role (allows File Gateway to write objects into S3).
Review file share mount command (`mount -t nfs -o hard :/saa-file-gateway-bridge-[account-id] /mnt/s3`) and click Create.

consoleSteps.note: File Gateway automatically generates an IAM role that grants S3 read/write permissions.

consoleSteps.title: Test File Mount, Local Caching, and Automatic S3 Sync

instructions.text: Connect to a Linux client machine on the same network.
Mount the NFS file share: sudo mount -t nfs -o hard :/saa-file-gateway-bridge-[account-id] /mnt/s3.
Write a test file: echo "Hello Hybrid Cloud" > /mnt/s3/hybrid-test.txt.
Open Amazon S3 Console -> Open saa-file-gateway-bridge-[account-id].
Verify that hybrid-test.txt appears instantly as a native S3 object.

consoleSteps.note: Files written to NFS/SMB shares are stored directly as native objects in Amazon S3.

consoleSteps.title: Tear down lab resources in dependency order

instructions.text: Unmount NFS share on client: sudo umount /mnt/s3.
Open Storage Gateway -> Select file share -> Choose Actions -> Delete file share.
Select gateway saa-s3-file-gateway -> Choose Actions -> Delete gateway.
Terminate the EC2 Storage Gateway instance.
Delete test objects and delete S3 bucket saa-file-gateway-bridge-[account-id].

cheatSheet.title: Storage Gateway Types
cheatSheet.body: S3 File Gateway: NFS/SMB file shares to native S3 objects. FSx File Gateway: SMB shares to FSx for Windows. Volume Gateway: iSCSI block storage (Cached vs Stored). Tape Gateway: iSCSI Virtual Tape Library to Glacier.

cheatSheet.title: File Gateway vs Volume Gateway
cheatSheet.body: Use S3 File Gateway for file protocol access (NFS/SMB) storing native S3 objects. Use Volume Gateway for block storage (iSCSI EBS snapshots).

cheatSheet.title: Local Caching
cheatSheet.body: Storage Gateway uses dedicated local disk storage to buffer low-latency read/write operations before syncing to AWS.

troubleshooting.title: NFS Mount Connection Timeout
troubleshooting.body: Ensure client Security Group allows outbound TCP/UDP port 2049 (NFS) to the Storage Gateway instance IP address.

troubleshooting.title: Gateway Activation Failure
troubleshooting.body: Verify port 80 (HTTP) is temporarily open for initial activation from your browser to the Storage Gateway IP.

examTraps.title: File vs Block Protocol Traps
examTraps.body: If an exam question mentions legacy NFS or SMB file shares, do NOT choose Volume Gateway (iSCSI); choose S3 File Gateway.

examTraps.title: Tape Library Replacement
examTraps.body: If an exam question mentions replacing physical tape backups (e.g., Veeam, NetBackup), choose Tape Gateway.

title: Automated Online File Migration with AWS DataSync
goal: Goal: Automate rapid online file transfer and ongoing synchronization between on-premises NFS/SMB shares and AWS storage (S3, EFS, FSx) using AWS DataSync.

concepts.title: AWS DataSync Overview
concepts.body: An online data transfer service that automates and accelerates moving data between on-premises storage (NFS, SMB, HDFS) and AWS storage (S3, EFS, FSx) over the network.

concepts.title: DataSync Agent Appliance
concepts.body: A virtual machine deployed on-premises (VMware, KVM, Hyper-V, or EC2) that reads local files, compresses/encrypts data, and streams it to AWS at up to 10 Gbps.

concepts.title: DataSync vs DMS vs MGN
concepts.body: AWS DataSync: Online file/object storage migration (NFS, SMB, EFS, S3). AWS DMS: Database row-level schema & table replication. AWS MGN: Block-level host OS disk server rehosting.

concepts.title: Data Integrity & Verification
concepts.body: DataSync automatically calculates TLS checksums during transit and compares source vs destination file metadata to verify 100% data integrity.

concepts.title: AWS Migration Services Decision Matrix
concepts.body: Migration ServiceLayer / ProtocolPrimary SourcePrimary TargetKey FeatureAWS DataSyncFile & Object (NFS/SMB)On-prem NFS/SMB/S3Amazon S3, EFS, FSxFast online network sync up to 10 GbpsAWS MGNBlock Storage (OS Disks)Physical / Virtual ServersAmazon EC2 InstancesBlock-level host rehosting (Lift & Shift)AWS DMSDatabase Rows & TablesRelational / NoSQL DBsAmazon RDS, Aurora, DynamoDBRow-level DB migration + CDC replicationAWS Snowball EdgeOffline Bulk StorageOn-prem Datacenter (10TB+)Amazon S3 BucketsOffline physical appliance shipping

whyItMatters: This matters because SAA-C03 exam questions frequently test choosing the exact right migration tool: DataSync for online file transfers, DMS for databases, and MGN for server rehosting.
costWarning: DataSync transfer, task, storage, network and connected-service charges may apply.

consoleSteps.title: Create Source and Target Amazon S3 Buckets

instructions.text: Open Amazon S3 -> Choose Create bucket.
Create Source bucket: saa-datasync-source-[account-id] in us-east-1.
Create Target bucket: saa-datasync-target-[account-id] in us-east-1.
Upload a sample file datasync-sample.txt into the Source bucket.

consoleSteps.note: Using two S3 buckets allows simulating full DataSync online transfer tasks at $0 cost.

consoleSteps.title: Create DataSync Source Location

instructions.text: Open AWS DataSync Console -> Choose Locations -> Click Create location.
Select Location type Amazon S3.
Select Region us-east-1.
Select S3 bucket saa-datasync-source-[account-id].
Choose Autogenerate IAM role (grants DataSync permission to read source objects).
Choose Create location.

consoleSteps.note: DataSync locations store connection configurations for on-prem NFS/SMB shares or AWS S3/EFS/FSx.

consoleSteps.title: Create DataSync Target Location

instructions.text: In DataSync Locations, choose Create location.
Select Location type Amazon S3.
Select Region us-east-1.
Select S3 bucket saa-datasync-target-[account-id].
Choose Autogenerate IAM role (grants DataSync permission to write target objects).
Choose Create location.

consoleSteps.note: Target location points to the destination S3 bucket, EFS file system, or FSx share.

consoleSteps.title: Create DataSync Transfer Task with Bandwidth & Schedule Settings

instructions.text: Open DataSync -> Choose Tasks -> Click Create task.
Select existing Source location saa-datasync-source-[account-id].
Select existing Target location saa-datasync-target-[account-id].
Set Task name to saa-datasync-sync-task.
Under Task configuration, set Bandwidth limit to 10 MB/s (throttling control).
Under Data verification, keep Verify only the data transferred selected.
Under Schedule, select Every day (or keep manual execution).
Choose Create task.

consoleSteps.note: Bandwidth limits prevent DataSync from consuming all available WAN upload capacity.

consoleSteps.title: Execute DataSync Task and Verify Data Integrity

instructions.text: Select task saa-datasync-sync-task -> Click Start -> Choose Start with default settings.
Monitor Task execution status transitioning: Preparing → Transferring → Verifying → Success.
Open Amazon S3 Console -> Open target bucket saa-datasync-target-[account-id].
Confirm datasync-sample.txt appears with matching metadata and checksums.

consoleSteps.note: DataSync verifies object checksums in transit to guarantee 100% data integrity.

consoleSteps.title: Tear down lab resources in dependency order

instructions.text: Select DataSync task saa-datasync-sync-task -> Choose Actions -> Delete.
Select source and target DataSync locations -> Choose Actions -> Delete.
Delete test objects and delete both S3 buckets saa-datasync-source-[account-id] and saa-datasync-target-[account-id].

cheatSheet.title: AWS DataSync Overview
cheatSheet.body: Accelerated online network file transfer service for NFS, SMB, HDFS to Amazon S3, EFS, and FSx up to 10 Gbps.

cheatSheet.title: DataSync vs Storage Gateway
cheatSheet.body: DataSync: Data migration and periodic batch sync tool. Storage Gateway: Continuous hybrid cloud storage bridge with local read/write caching.

cheatSheet.title: DataSync vs Snowball
cheatSheet.body: DataSync: Online network transfer over WAN. Snowball Edge: Offline physical appliance shipping when network bandwidth is too slow for 10+ TB.

troubleshooting.title: DataSync Agent Offline
troubleshooting.body: Ensure outbound TCP port 443 (HTTPS) to AWS DataSync service endpoints is open on on-premises firewall.

troubleshooting.title: Task Execution Failed: Access Denied

examTraps.title: DataSync vs DMS Usage
examTraps.body: Do NOT select DataSync for database migrations. DataSync is for file systems (NFS/SMB/EFS/S3). Select AWS DMS for database tables.

examTraps.title: DataSync vs MGN Usage
examTraps.body: Do NOT select DataSync to migrate host OS boot volumes or rehost EC2 instances. Select AWS MGN for server rehosting.

title: Create a Direct Connect private VIF and test VPC routing
goal: Goal: Create a private virtual interface for Direct Connect and route private traffic to a VPC.

concepts.title: Private VIF
concepts.body: A private virtual interface connects Direct Connect to private AWS resources through a VGW or Direct Connect gateway.

concepts.title: Direct Connect gateway
concepts.body: A Direct Connect gateway can connect a private VIF to one or more VPCs through gateway associations.

whyItMatters: This matters because Direct Connect is private dedicated connectivity. It is not encrypted by default and is different from VPN over the internet.

consoleSteps.title: Set up the lab user and permissions

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console with an IAM user, IAM role, or IAM Identity Center permission set.
Sign in to the AWS Management Console using an IAM user or lab role with VPC permissions.
Sign in to the AWS Management Console using an IAM user or lab role with VPC permissions.
For least privilege, use the grouped permissions below.

consoleSteps.note: Identity check: sts:GetCallerIdentity Direct Connect read: directconnect:DescribeConnections, directconnect:DescribeVirtualInterfaces, directconnect:DescribeDirectConnectGateways Direct Connect setup: directconnect:CreatePrivateVirtualInterface, directconnect:CreateDirectConnectGateway, directconnect:CreateDirectConnectGatewayAssociation, directconnect:DeleteVirtualInterface VPC gateway and routes: ec2:CreateVpnGateway, ec2:AttachVpnGateway, ec2:CreateRoute, ec2:DescribeRouteTables Cleanup: directconnect:DeleteDirectConnectGatewayAssociation, directconnect:DeleteDirectConnectGateway, ec2:DetachVpnGateway, ec2:DeleteVpnGateway
consoleSteps.warning: Do not leave broad admin access or long-term access keys in real company accounts.

consoleSteps.title: Confirm you have a Direct Connect connection

instructions.text: Open Direct Connect.
Choose Connections.
Confirm an active dedicated or hosted connection exists.
Do not create paid Direct Connect resources unless this is a real lab account.

consoleSteps.warning: This task cannot fully work without an existing Direct Connect connection and on-prem router setup.

consoleSteps.title: Create a Direct Connect gateway

instructions.text: Open Direct Connect → Direct Connect gateways.
Choose Create Direct Connect gateway.
Name: saa-vpc-task19-dxgw.
Amazon-side ASN: use 64512 for this example.

consoleSteps.note: Use an ASN that does not conflict with your network.

consoleSteps.title: Create or confirm the VPC Virtual Private Gateway

instructions.text: Open VPC → Virtual private gateways.
Create saa-vpc-task19-vgw if needed.
Attach it to the lab VPC.
Associate the VGW with the Direct Connect gateway.

consoleSteps.note: Allowed prefixes should include the VPC CIDR.

consoleSteps.title: Create the private virtual interface

instructions.text: Open Direct Connect → Virtual interfaces.
Choose Create virtual interface.
Type: Private.
Connection: choose the active connection.
Gateway: choose the Direct Connect gateway.
Enter VLAN, BGP ASN, and peer IPs from your network plan.

consoleSteps.warning: Wrong VLAN or BGP peer values stop routing from working.

consoleSteps.title: Update route tables and test

instructions.text: Open VPC → Route tables.
Add the on-prem CIDR route to the VGW if needed.
Confirm BGP routes are advertised on the router.
Test private IP traffic between on-prem and a private EC2 instance.

consoleSteps.note: Security groups and on-prem firewalls must allow the test traffic.

consoleSteps.title: Tear down in dependency order

instructions.text: Delete or disable the private VIF if created for a lab.
Delete the Direct Connect gateway association.
Delete the Direct Connect gateway if created for a lab.
Remove VPC routes to on-prem.
Detach and delete the VGW if created for this lab.

consoleSteps.warning: Do not delete production Direct Connect resources.

cliSteps.expectedResult: Expected: the chosen connection is available or ordering.

cliSteps.title: Template private VIF command

commands.text:
cat > private-vif.json <<'EOF'
{
  "virtualInterfaceName": "saa-vpc-task19-private-vif",
  "vlan": 101,
  "asn": 65000,
  "authKey": "CHANGE-ME",
  "amazonAddress": "169.254.100.1/30",
  "customerAddress": "169.254.100.2/30",
  "addressFamily": "ipv4",
  "directConnectGatewayId": "REPLACE-DXGW-ID"
}
EOF
aws directconnect create-private-virtual-interface --region $REGION --connection-id $DX_CONNECTION_ID --new-private-virtual-interface file://private-vif.json

cliSteps.warning: Edit the JSON with real VLAN, ASN, BGP key, peer IPs, and DXGW ID before running.

cliSteps.title: Verify VIF state
cliSteps.note: Expected: VIF eventually becomes available when accepted/configured.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Expected: VIF eventually becomes available when accepted/configured.

cliSteps.title: Cleanup reminder

commands.text:
# Replace with the VIF ID created for this lab only
VIF_ID=dxvif-xxxxxxxx
aws directconnect delete-virtual-interface --region $REGION --virtual-interface-id $VIF_ID

cliSteps.warning: Do not delete shared or production Direct Connect resources.

verification.text: Virtual Private Cloud configuration verified in Amazon VPC.

cleanup.text: Delete subnets, route tables, Internet Gateways, and the custom VPC created during this lab.

troubleshooting.title: No Direct Connect connection
troubleshooting.body: You cannot create a working private VIF without an active dedicated or hosted connection.

troubleshooting.title: BGP down
troubleshooting.body: Check VLAN, ASN, BGP auth key, and peer IP addresses.

troubleshooting.title: Traffic still fails
troubleshooting.body: Check VPC routes, allowed prefixes, security groups, NACLs, and on-prem firewall rules.

examTraps.title: Direct Connect is not encrypted by default
examTraps.body: Use VPN over Direct Connect or app encryption if encryption is required.

examTraps.title: Private VIF is for private resources
examTraps.body: Use private VIF for VPC private connectivity, not public AWS service endpoints.

examTraps.title: Transit VIF differs from private VIF
examTraps.body: Transit VIF is used with Transit Gateway through a Direct Connect gateway.
